p: shall we say then: He passes now to another benefit of Christ, which is called sanctification or regeneration.

sin: In that corruption, for though the guiltiness of sin, is not imputed to us, yet the corruption still remains in us: and this is killed little by little by the sanctification that follows justification.

How shall we: The benefits of justification and sanctification are always inseparable joined together, and both of them proceed from Christ by the grace of God: now sanctification is the abolishing of sin, that is, of our natural corruption, whose place is taken by the cleanness and pureness of a reformed nature.

dead to sin: They are said by Paul to be dead to sin, who are made partakers of the power of Christ, so that the natural corruption is dead in them, that is, the power of it is removed, and it does not bring forth its bitter fruits: and on the other hand, they are said to live to sin, who are in the flesh, that is, whom the Spirit of God has not delivered from the slavery of the corruption of nature.

Know ye not: There are three parts of this sanctification: that is, the death of the old man or sin, his burial, and the resurrection of the new man, descending into us from the virtue of the death, burial, and resurrection of Christ, of which benefit our baptism is a sign and pledge.
Jesus Christ were baptized into his: To the end that growing up as one with him, we should receive his strength to extinguish sin in us, and to make us new men.
by the glory of the Father: So that Christ himself, being released of his infirmity and weakness, might live in glory with God forever.

we also should walk in newness: And we who are his members rise for this purpose, that being made partakers of the very same power, we should begin to lead a new life, as though we were already in heaven.

For if we have been planted: The death of sin and the life of righteousness, or our ingrafting into Christ, and growing up into one with him, cannot be separated by any means, neither in death nor life: by which it follows that no man is sanctified who lives still to sin, and therefore is no man made partaker of Christ by faith, who does not repent and turn from his wickedness: for as he said before, the law is not overturned but established by faith.
likeness of his death: And by means of the strength which comes from him to us, so we die to sin, as he is dead.
be also in the likeness of: For every day we become more perfect: for we will never be perfectly sanctified, as long as we live here.

old man is crucified with: Our entire nature, as we are conceived and born into this world with sin, is called "old", partly by comparing that old Adam with Christ, and partly also in respect of the deformed state of our corrupt nature, which we change with a new.
him: Our corrupt nature is regarded as belonging to Christ, not because of what he has done, but by imputation.
body of sin might be destroyed: That wickedness which remains in us.
serve sin: The end of sanctification which we aim at, and will at length come to, that is, when God will be all in all.
For he that is dead is: He proves it by the effects of death, comparing Christ the head with his members.
once: Once for all.
God: With God.
Let not sin therefore: An exhortation to contend and strive with corruption and all the effects of it.
reign in your mortal body: By reigning Paul means that principal and high rule which no man strives against, and even if anyone does, it is in vain.
yield ye your: To sin, as to a Lord or tyrant.
members as: Your mind and all the powers of it.
instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: As instruments to commit wickedness with them.

For sin shall not have dominion: He grants that sin is not yet so dead in us that it is utterly extinct: but he promises victory to those that contend bravely, because we have the grace of God given to us which works so that the law is not now in us the power and instrument of sin.

What then: To be under the law and under sin signifies the same thing, with respect to whose who are not sanctified, and on the other hand to be under grace and righteousness is in harmony with those that are regenerated. Now these are contraries, so that one cannot agree with the other: therefore let righteousness expel sin.
But God be thanked: By nature we are slaves to sin and free from righteousness, but by the grace of God we are made servants to righteousness, and therefore free from sin.

form of doctrine which was delivered: This type of speech has a special meaning in it: for he means by this that the doctrine of the gospel is like a certain mould in which we are cast, to be shaped and fashioned like it.
free from righteousness: Righteousness had no rule over you.
What fruit had ye then in: An exhortation to the study of righteousness and hatred of sin, the contrary results of both being set down before us.
end of those things is death: The reward or payment.
For the wages of sin is: Death is the punishment due to sin, but we are sanctified freely, to everlasting life.
